sections.content: How many people are "assemblers (electrical and electronic products)"?

20,970 people

were counted on the census as "assemblers (electrical and electronic products)" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Assemblers of electrical and electronic products wire prepared parts and/or sub-assemblies in the manufacture of electrical and electronic equipment, make coils and wiring harnesses, and assemble previously prepared parts in the production of electrical and electronic goods and components.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "assemblers (electrical and electronic products)" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "assemblers (electrical and electronic products)", 13.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "assemblers (electrical and electronic products)" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "assemblers (electrical and electronic products)" included:

  • textile process operatives
  • fishmongers and poultry dressers
  • metal machining setters and setter-operators

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "assemblers (electrical and electronic products)" there were more men than women (61.6% compared with 38.4%).

This means "assemblers (electrical and electronic products)" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "process, plant and machine operatives".

Men made up 61.6% and women made up 38.4% of "assemblers (electrical and electronic products)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "assemblers (electrical and electronic products)" included:

  • management consultants and business analysts
  • sales accounts and business development managers
  • functional managers and directors (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "assemblers (electrical and electronic products)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "assemblers (electrical and electronic products)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "assemblers (electrical and electronic products)", 9.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (89.1% compared with 10.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (96%) than self-employed (4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included County Durham, this is in the region of the North East.
